facts.subject: Quest experience rewards
facts.statement: The wiki's fixed-Defence-XP table lists exactly 13 quest/miniquest rewards, from A Soul's Bane (500) to King's Ransom (33,000). A quest not on it gives no fixed Defence XP. Choosable lamps and optional rewards (e.g. Daero's Monkey Madness I training) are not in this table and must never go to Defence for this build.
facts.caveat: The table covers fixed quest rewards only. Optional post-quest training (Monkey Madness I Daero: 20,000 or 35,000 Defence if accepted) and choosable lamps (e.g. Black Knights' Fortress, Mudfoot's Big Adventure combat lamps) can also add Defence, so the planners must decline or redirect them. Defence 50 = 101,333 XP and Defence 51 = 111,945 XP (tools/xp.py), so total Defence XP must stay below 111,945.

The wiki says dying to any form is safe for regular hardcore ironmen, but that hardcore group ironmen must be concerned about dying in the first three forms. Hardcore Worlds uses the HGIM death ruleset, so forms 1-3 must be treated as potentially run-ending. The 4th-form death is scripted.
facts.caveat: Resolves the researcher's doubt: the 4th-form max hit of 1 is not an anomaly. That form attacks every game tick (0.6 s) for exactly 1, drains prayer, and has 255 HP. The third form has a 10-minute time limit. A ring of life sends you back to spawn and resets him to form 1. If he stays idle too long he resets to form 1. On HW, death safety for forms 1-3 needs a Threat-desk ruling (RFI-01 already open).

sources.title: Koschei the deathless
sources.quote: Dying to any of his forms are safe deaths (including for [[Hardcore ironmen]]), though players must die to his fourth form (or defeat it) to get the vote. Only [[Hardcore group ironmen]] need to be concerned about dying to the first three forms, as dying to the fourth form is a scripted safe death.

facts.subject: Werewolf Agility Course
facts.statement: On the Werewolf Agility Course the deathslide is the only obstacle that can be failed.
